qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High-voltage cable qualification barriers and multi-year order backlogs for European grid interconnectors and offshore wind; however, multi-cycle capital returns fail the 12% hurdle (RoCE was -3% in 2020, 3% in 2021, 7% in 2022; 5Y median ~7%) and capital intensity is high. Primary erosion threats include lump-sum EPC contract execution risks, offshore wind project cancellations or timing delays, and cyclical capacity additions from peers.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power). While NKT benefits from multi-year backlogs in high-voltage offshore wind interconnectors, its 5-year median RoCE is ~7% (operating near break-even to low single digits between 2019-2022 before the recent 2023-2024 capacity squeeze). The business has historically lacked through-cycle pricing power above inflation and requires heavy ongoing capital reinvestment for specialized manufacturing and cable-laying vessels.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle profitability: RoCE was -3% (2020), 3% (2021), 7% (2022), 20% (2023), and 35% (2024), resulting in a 5-year median of ~7%, well below the 12% GAAP ROIC hurdle. Revenue is concentrated in high-voltage turnkey solutions, medium-voltage cables, and telecom cables. While the current European grid build-out has created tight capacity and record backlogs, historical operating performance demonstrates high cyclicality, execution risks on turnkey installation contracts, and vulnerability to offshore wind developer financing delays.
